name: Blue-Grey
lede: Blue-grey is a plain English compound for a grey with blue in it, and the swatch used for it here, a clear light blue, is only one of at least five competing versions.

sections.title: Five blue-greys
sections.body:
Our library holds five screen values under this name: the swatch #6699CC from Wikipedia's list, a RAL 7031 value (#5D6970), and three from the xkcd color survey [1]. The swatch is the bluest of them, a clear light blue with a chroma of about 32, and ISCC-NBS (1955) calls its nearest block simply "light blue" [1]. The RAL value is a dark slate that sits 22.3 units from it, and the xkcd greys lie between 8 and 13 units away [1].

The same swatch also appears as Livid, in Wikipedia, ISCC-NBS and Maerz and Paul, and Crayola's Cerulean Frost is 2.1 units from it [1]. The nearest name in our teaching set is [[cornflower]], 4.2 away [1]. If you want the greyer reading, look at [[grey-blue]], [[dove-grey]] and [[gunmetal]].

sections.title: A name with soft edges
sections.body: Two broad words joined together make a color with no fixed edge. Batchelor points out that Literary Welsh has no words that match English green, blue, grey or brown exactly, which is a reminder that these boundaries are a language's habit, not nature's [2]. Paterson glosses Dutch blue as a blue-grey and gunmetal as a dull blue-grey [3], and St Clair calls gunmetal a mid blue-gray and [[cadet-blue]] a gray-greenish blue taken from military uniforms [4].

sections.title: In paint and in fashion
sections.body:
Medieval illuminators used blue-gray tones in grisaille miniatures to show water, atmosphere, light and distance, as in a manuscript made around 1460 for Philip the Good of Burgundy [5]. Gage notes that a beautiful blue-grey, made by laying transparent black over a white ground, had long been known in the studio [6]. He also reports that Matisse's *Red Studio* (1911) was originally a blue-grey interior, and traces of that show through its thinner paint [6]. The Pigment Compendium lists blue grey as a synonym for blue lead, a mixed pigment based on lead compounds and named for its color [7].

Blue-gray later worked quietly as a social color. After the French Revolution, Greenfield writes, quieter blues (sky blue, gray blues, navy) found buyers across all classes, and they fitted Victorian ideas of propriety [8].

Painters also use it as a foil. Gurney describes a low-chroma blue-gray as the complementary accent to high-chroma reds, oranges and yellows, and deep blue-gray as the color of shadows under warm light [9]. Look for it on a dark-haired man's lower face: hair follicles give it a blue-gray cast [9].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
The swatch is rare as a painted color. A color within six units of it covers at least five per cent of the canvas in only 66 of 23,781 paintings, about 0.3 per cent [10]. It is twice as likely in the 1900s as the average, and the 1660s stand out, with 7 of 820 canvases [10]. Alfred Sisley and Henri Matisse each have 3 of 50 works in range, more than 20 times the archive average [10]. Sisley's [[painting:commons-Q17493189|*The Bridge at Moret*]] (1893) fills 30 per cent of its canvas, and a Mughal portrait of Prince Azam Shah, of about 1660, 51 per cent [10].

In the paintings that hold it, it is most often a mid-tone (55 per cent) or a highlight (42 per cent), almost never a shadow [10]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, and the swatch is a light blue, so the greyer blue-greys in the books are not what these matches measure [10][1]. In print, *blue grey* peaks around 1949 [11].

origin.named_after: English compound of blue and grey; no single coinage is documented
origin.first_recorded: origin undocumented; the earliest dated source for this name in our library is RAL (1927)

disambiguation.gloss: a gray-greenish blue named for military uniforms

questions.q: Why is this page's swatch a poor guide to what most people mean by blue-grey?
choices: It is a fairly clear light blue, while the other versions are much duller
It is actually a pale green
It is a purple-grey from RAL
It was made for Crayola in 1990
questions.answer: It is a fairly clear light blue, while the other versions are much duller

questions.q: What did medieval illuminators use blue-gray tones in grisaille miniatures to show?
True or false: in our archive, a color matching this swatch fills a large part of more than one painting in ten.

openers: Our library holds five different screen colors under the name blue-grey, from a clear light blue to a dark slate.
Matisse's Red Studio started out as a blue-grey interior, and some of it still shows through.
Look at a dark-haired man's lower face: hair follicles give it a blue-gray cast.

issues: Swatch is a light blue, not a grey: said plainly; greyer alternatives given with CIEDE2000 distances.
